HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. LAYOUT (master of the set): close two-shot in strict profile, the two faces meeting at the exact centre of the frame. The MAN on the LEFT, head bowed to her, one hand flat at the small of her back; the WOMAN on the RIGHT, up on her toes, both hands in his hair, pulling him down into the kiss. Their bodies make one shape; behind them the place dissolves into soft painted bokeh. One key light from the side rakes both faces. Here: night rain outside a back wall, two horses waiting in the dark behind, drain-mud on her chin, rain on both faces, Manmyung in a soaked noble hanbok, Seohyun in a dark travel coat. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = seohyeon, SECOND face = manmyung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). KIM SEOHYUN — Look: Gentle long face, apologetic eyes, a careful mouth; a softer cousin of young Yushin's face, never the same man. Completely clean-shaven and long-haired when young (loose topknot, long strands past the jaw); a thin moustache and short beard from his forties. Now: Young official in his twenties, CLEAN-SHAVEN, no beard or moustache: steel-blue silk po, white collar, dark sash, jougwan cap over a loose topknot with long loose strands. Colour #3E8EF0. MANMYUNG — Look: Young royal Kim noblewoman whose face runs in the family: mostly her granddaughter Gotaso's (oval face, bright almond eyes, small nose, cheerful sly mouth) with a touch of her daughter Munhee's long jaw and arched brows; one eyebrow up, a closed-mouth smirk. Black hair in a high round bun with loose strands at the temples, one gold binyeo with a red bead, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Short white silk jeogori with deep crimson collar ribbon and cuffs, long deep-crimson chima with a gold-embroidered waistband, a pale celadon-green shawl; good silk she will ruin in the rain. Colour #c98bb9. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
